physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's system is a 3x3x3 3D stack with TSV and bonding-layer thermal resistivities and a heat sink on top, so it needs a layered 3D thermal model. A 2D single-layer or interposer-style Studio model cannot represent inter-layer heat flow, TSV conduction, bonding/TIM layers, or the per-layer temperature results in Figure 10.

The Monolithic vs TSV comparison depends on removing bonding layers and modifying TSV-area thermal resistivity (Table 3: Copper 0.0025 mK/W, TIM 0.25 mK/W, TSV area 0.0226 mK/W). These material and layer assumptions cannot be reproduced in a planar model.

The paper gives no router coordinates or per-router watts as text, since the per-router synthetic-benchmark powers are only in Figure 8. It publishes only router size, per-router static power and energy per bit, and traffic-scaled power charts. No complete same-scenario floorplan and power set exists.

The paper reports reliability (Black's model MTTF) as a primary outcome. The setup is not a controller or optimizer study, so there is no controller or optimizer to compare, and reliability calculations exceed a simple thermal setup.
The HotSpot 6.0 configuration (heat sink, package, convection, ambient, layer thicknesses) is not published in full, so the solver setup cannot be matched.
